description: A strong earthquake strikes an urban area while you are inside a multi-storey building. Make the right calls, in order, to keep yourself and others safe.
objectives: Respond correctly to the initial shaking (Drop, Cover, Hold On)
Evacuate correctly and behave safely at the assembly point

steps.title: The Shaking Begins
steps.narrative: You are on the 4th floor of an office building. The floor starts shaking violently. Furniture rattles. What do you do in the first few seconds?

options.text: Run toward the elevator to get out fast
options.mistake: Elevators can fail or trap you during an earthquake — never use them during or right after shaking.

options.text: Stand near the window to see what's happening
options.mistake: Windows can shatter and glass is a major injury risk during shaking.

options.text: Drop, Cover, and Hold On under a sturdy desk
Run down the stairs immediately while it's still shaking
options.mistake: Moving through a shaking building increases your risk of falling or being hit by debris.

steps.title: Still Shaking
steps.narrative: The shaking continues and a light fixture crashes to the ground a few metres away. What now?

options.text: Stay covered and hold on until the shaking fully stops
Get up to move to what looks like a safer spot
options.mistake: Moving during active shaking is when most injuries happen — stay covered until it stops.

steps.title: The Shaking Stops
steps.narrative: The shaking has stopped. Dust is settling. What should you do next?

options.text: Check yourself and people nearby for injuries before moving
Immediately sprint for the nearest exit
options.mistake: Rushing without checking for injuries or hazards can make things worse for you and others.

options.text: Go back to your desk to grab your belongings
options.mistake: Personal belongings are not worth the delay or risk — prioritize safety first.

steps.title: Hazard Check
steps.narrative: You smell something like gas near the kitchen area. What is the correct response?

options.text: Avoid open flames/switches, report it, and move away from the area
Try to locate and fix the leak yourself
options.mistake: Attempting to fix a gas leak yourself is dangerous — leave it to trained personnel and move away.
Ignoring a possible gas leak risks fire or explosion — it must be treated seriously.

steps.title: Evacuation Decision
steps.narrative: Building wardens announce an evacuation. The stairwell is intact but crowded. How do you proceed?

options.text: Use the stairs calmly, keeping to one side, helping anyone who needs it
Push through the crowd to exit faster
options.mistake: Pushing through crowds during an evacuation increases the risk of falls and injuries for everyone.

options.text: Wait alone in the office until the crowd clears
options.mistake: Delaying evacuation without reason increases exposure to aftershock risk.

steps.title: At the Assembly Point
steps.narrative: You're outside at the designated assembly point. Aftershocks are possible. What's the right behavior now?

options.text: Stay in the open away from buildings, report your status, and wait for official instructions
Head back inside to check on the building
options.mistake: Re-entering a shaken building before it's cleared by authorities risks injury from aftershocks or structural damage.

options.text: Leave the assembly area immediately to go home without informing anyone
options.mistake: Leaving without checking in makes it harder for responders to know everyone is accounted for.
